result.note: Tested the EU Commission's proposed metal-scrap exclusion of India and the US sanctions law's tariff mechanism; skipped the monthly oil-import figures as transient.

questions.prompt: In September 2026, the European Commission proposed a measure on metal-scrap imports affecting India. Consider the following statements about the proposal:
items: It would exclude India from EU metal-scrap imports from May 2026.
It cites weak recycling controls as the reason for the exclusion.
The draft was open to consultation until 16 October 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong: the exclusion would apply from May 2027, not May 2026. The draft is not yet a hard measure and remains open to consultation, so it works as leverage held in reserve.
questions.source: the European Commission proposed excluding India from EU metal-scrap imports from May 2027, citing weak recycling controls

questions.prompt: In September 2026, US President Donald Trump signed a Russia and Iran sanctions law. Consider the following statements about its implications for India:
items: It exposes India to tariffs of up to 100% on purchases of Russian energy.
The tariffs apply automatically, without needing a presidential trigger.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the tariff needs a presidential trigger, so it is not yet a hard duty. Meanwhile India's Russian oil imports fell 16.5% in August 2026, though Russia remained India's top supplier.
questions.source: Trump signed the Russia and Iran sanctions law exposing India to tariffs up to 100% on Russian-energy purchases
